THE DEFECT (live-reproduced by the evaluator): in sync_coverage() the 'unknown_category' and 'unknown_source' branches 'continue' WITHOUT adding category_id to declared_category_ids, so the prune loop treats a still-declared pair as no-longer-declared and DELETES its row. Repro: sync Cloudflare -> 14 rows; rename the two referenced source slugs in the DB; re-sync -> {unchanged: 12, unknown_source: 2, withdrawn: 2}, rows 14 -> 12, and serverless-functions + containers-app-hosting regress to undeclared/'unknown' in the public API. Restoring the slugs and re-syncing returns 14.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the silent prune dropped Cloudflare's evidence-backed count from 3 (exactly the Q9-A floor) to 1 with NO hard failure. The Q9-A floor was enforced only as a CONFIG-LOAD invariant, never as a DATABASE invariant, so the catalogue could erode below the floor while every individual surviving row stayed legal.

TIGHT SCOPE, NO MIGRATION. Alembic head stays 0011_provider_category_coverage. Every S2 guardrail still binds: no new runtime or test dependency (Q6-A); no Redis; no live network (Q3-A); no credentialed provider API (Q5-A); no secrets; no FTS; Q11 unchanged (derivation stays computed, never stored); region/residency stay out of scope (Q8-A).

Four further evaluator observations are tracked follow-ups and are explicitly NOT in scope here: (B) staleness masking a genuine free-tier withdrawal (needs an owner product ruling); (C) a (verified_free, unknown) pair staying silent forever; (D) contradiction-reader fragility against new Wave-3 ReviewItem producers; (E) _applied_revisions() asserting the script graph rather than the DB.

REMEDIATION r1 after a Level-2 FAIL on head b904134 (5 of 6 criteria PASSed; criterion 2 failed). F-1: only the source axis was fixed, and the comment justifying the omission was false -- the FK's ON DELETE CASCADE covers a DELETED category but not a RENAMED one, so the row survived and was pruned (14->13, backed 3->2). F-2: an undisclosed 'if not rows: return' made 20% erosion raise while 100% erosion stayed silent. F-3: the docs were widened to assert behaviour that was not implemented, which the product-truth rule forbids.

The category axis is fixed by ATTRIBUTION, not registration: an unresolved category slug makes every unattributed row ambiguous, so the prune is suppressed for the whole run. This errs toward retaining a row that could have been withdrawn, which is the correct side to err on given 'a resolution failure is not a withdrawal' and 'unknown is better than guessed'.

The savepoint hardening (making the rollback guarantee local to sync_provider rather than a property of its callers) is deliberately NOT in this PR. It is a separate follow-up off fresh main, so this remediation stays ~3 lines against an otherwise-passing evaluation.
objective: Make a declared coverage row survive a reference this sync cannot resolve, on BOTH the source and the category axis, and make the Q9-A evidence floor a DATABASE invariant rather than only a config-load one. Concretely: (a) an unresolvable 'source' reference still resolves its category, so the pair is registered as declared BEFORE any resolution step that can fail and the stored row is left intact; (b) an unresolvable CATEGORY slug cannot be registered at all -- not having an id is the definition of that branch -- so withdrawal becomes unattributable and the prune is suppressed wholesale for that run rather than deleting a row it cannot prove was withdrawn; (c) after the upsert and the prune, sync_coverage() re-reads the PERSISTED rows and asserts the same >= MIN_EVIDENCE_BACKED_COVERAGE floor that validate_coverage_floor() enforces at load, raising CoverageFloorError on a shortfall, with zero rows treated as the MAXIMAL erosion rather than an exemption; and (d) the unknown_category / unknown_source outcomes stay in the returned counts so the condition remains observable.
scope: apps/api/app/ingest/config_sync.py: move 'declared_category_ids.add(category_id)' ABOVE the source-resolution step, so neither the unknown_category nor the unknown_source branch can reach the prune loop with the pair unregistered. A failure to resolve a reference is not a withdrawal of the declaration.

risks: Raising on a floor shortfall aborts the caller's transaction, which is a deliberately louder failure mode than the previous silence. Mitigated by scoping the check to the provider being synced, by skipping it entirely on the documented pre-0010 no-op path where nothing is written, and by an actionable message naming the unresolved references. A pending review_item was rejected as the failure mode because it would record the erosion only AFTER committing it -- precisely the silent-degradation bug being fixed.

Wave 3 slices could trip the new raise if they onboard a provider against a partially-synced database. That is the intended behaviour: it is exactly the condition that silently eroded Cloudflare, and it now fails attributably at sync time instead of surfacing later as missing catalogue coverage.

The floor predicate is duplicated between config load and post-sync. Mitigated by sharing MIN_EVIDENCE_BACKED_COVERAGE and EVIDENCE_BACKED_COVERAGE_STATES and by a drift test pinning the two to the same constants.

Suppressing the prune wholesale on an unresolved category reference is deliberately blunt: a run with one bad slug performs no withdrawals at all. Accepted because coverage is mandatory over a fixed 14-slug taxonomy, so an unknown_category can only arise from DB drift and never from a legitimate config change -- and retaining a stale row is strictly safer than deleting a live one. The condition is observable via prune_suppressed and unresolved_categories.
